claims.text: The starting material is equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr in the as-cast state.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a high-temperature yield strength of 163–530 MPa.
Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen resistance.
Untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr suffers from pesting during high-temperature air exposure.
A thin aluminide coating can be applied to the alloy by pack cementation.
The aluminide coating will improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The aluminide treatment enriches the alloy surface in aluminum during high-temperature exposure.
Surface aluminum enrichment promotes in situ formation of a continuous, adherent Al2O3 scale.
The Al2O3 scale acts as a barrier to oxygen diffusion.
Reduced oxygen diffusion through the scale slows oxidation and pesting.
The coated alloy will have lower oxidation mass gain than untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
The coated alloy will exhibit less oxide-scale spallation than untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
A sufficiently thin aluminide coating will not alter the bulk microstructure controlling the alloy's mechanical properties.
The coated alloy will retain its room-temperature tensile ductility and high-temperature yield strength.
The proposed protection applies in air from 800 °C to 1000 °C for exposure durations of at least 5 hours.
The proposed protection applies under mechanical loading at strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.

contradictions.description: The boundary claims applicability for all durations of at least 5 hours, with no upper limit, while the uncertainty field states that long-term scale stability is unknown.
